title: Weapons Now Have Space Addresses
part1:
If weapons had address books, this news would rewrite one line in one of them. Their address is not on the ground, but in orbit.

On September 14, 2026, U.S. Secretary of the Air Force Troy Meink said that the United States was deploying space-control weapons in orbit to protect its joint forces from the actions of hostile parties.

According to an official U.S. government article, this was the first official statement admitting that the Space Force had deployed weapons in space. In other words, this news is not about announcing the name of a new weapon. It is about clearly showing the address of a weapon.
part2:
Until now, when people heard the words “weapons in space,” many probably imagined missiles flying up from the ground. They would be launched when needed and aimed at satellites overhead. It is an easy-to-understand scene of a space attack, often seen in movies.

In fact, on November 15, 2021, Russia destroyed one of its own satellites with a missile launched from the ground that rose directly to attack satellites. As a result, more than 1,500 pieces of space debris that could be tracked were created.

However, this was a destructive test in which a missile was launched from the ground. A missile flying through space and a weapon being placed in orbit are not the same thing.
part3:
What the United States acknowledged this time was the latter. Instead of a weapon on the ground flying into space, a weapon deployed in space protects the joint forces while staying there. Space becomes a place where weapons wait, rather than just a route they pass through.

Of course, no information has been made public about what the weapon can do, whether it has the ability to attack, or what targets it is meant for. This announcement alone does not mean that attacks from space have begun.

Even so, when the address of a weapon changes, the way we see space changes greatly. Satellites that support communications and location information also fly there. A change of address in the far-off sky is happening above our daily lives.
in_one_line: The United States acknowledged deploying weapons in orbit, turning space from a route into a place where weapons wait.
